title: USED TO
subtitle: Used to · antes solía…, antes hacía…

map.center: Usamos USED TO para hablar de hábitos y situaciones del pasado que ya no son así.

nodes.title: ¿Qué significa?
items: Algo que pasaba antes (muchas veces) y ahora no.
I used to play the piano. (Antes tocaba el piano.)

nodes.title: Afirmativa
items: Igual para todos: I / she / they used to

error.title: Error común

explain.es: Used to sirve para hablar de cosas que pasaban o eran verdad en el pasado y ya no lo son: hábitos repetidos (I used to play football every Saturday) y situaciones o estados (I used to have long hair). En español lo decimos con solía o con el pretérito imperfecto («jugaba, tenía»). Siempre lleva la idea de «antes sí… ahora no».
explain.en: Used to talks about past habits and states that are no longer true.

explain.title: 1 · Afirmativa
explain.es: Used to no cambia: es igual para todas las personas (I, you, he, she, we, they). Detrás va siempre el infinitivo sin to: used to play, nunca used to playing ni used to played. Se pronuncia /ˈjuːstə/: la d casi no suena («iústa»).
explain.en: Used to is the same for all persons and is followed by the infinitive. Pronunciation: /ˈjuːstə/.
formula: I / you / he / she / we / they + *used to* + infinitivo

examples.en: I used to play football every Saturday.
examples.es: Antes jugaba al fútbol todos los sábados.

examples.en: My dad used to have long hair. Can you believe it?
examples.es: Mi padre tenía el pelo largo. ¿Te lo puedes creer?

examples.en: We used to spend every summer at my grandparents' house.
examples.es: Pasábamos todos los veranos en casa de mis abuelos.

explain.title: 2 · Negativa
explain.es: Para la negativa usamos didn't + use to + infinitivo. ¡Ojo! Como didn't ya marca el pasado, use va sin -d: didn't use to. (Es la misma regla que didn't go, no didn't went.) También se puede decir never used to.
explain.en: Negative: didn't use to + infinitive (no -d after didn't). You can also say never used to.

examples.en: I didn't use to like vegetables, but now I love them.
examples.es: Antes no me gustaban las verduras, pero ahora me encantan.

examples.en: She didn't use to study much at school.
examples.es: Ella no estudiaba mucho en el colegio.

examples.en: We never used to go abroad on holiday.
examples.es: Nunca íbamos de vacaciones al extranjero.

explain.title: 3 · Preguntas
explain.es: Preguntas: (Wh-) + did + sujeto + use to + infinitivo? Otra vez use sin -d, porque ya está did. Respuestas cortas con did / didn't: Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.
explain.en: Questions: (Wh-) + did + subject + use to + verb? Short answers: Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.

examples.en: Did you use to wear glasses? — Yes, I did.
Where did you use to live before Madrid?
What did people use to do without mobile phones?

explain.title: Todo junto
head: Sujeto · Subject
✅ Afirmativa
⛔ Negativa
❓ Pregunta
💬 Respuesta corta
rows: Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.
Yes, you did. / No, you didn't.
Yes, she did. / No, she didn't.
Yes, we did. / No, we didn't.
Yes, they did. / No, they didn't.
explain.note: Truco: used (con d) solo en la afirmativa. Si hay did / didn't → use (sin d).
explain.note_en: used (with -d) only in the affirmative; with did / didn't → use.

explain.title: 4 · Hábitos y estados
explain.es: Used to vale para dos cosas: acciones repetidas (hábitos: play, go, eat, watch) y estados o situaciones que duraban (have, be, live, like, know). En los dos casos, ya no es así. Muy útil: there used to be = «antes había».
explain.en: Used to works for repeated actions (habits) and states (have, be, live, like). There used to be = there was before, but not now.
formula: Hábito + I used to + *go* + to the gym

examples.en: I used to watch cartoons every morning before school.
examples.es: Veía dibujos todas las mañanas antes del cole.

examples.en: He used to be really shy, but now he's a YouTuber.
examples.es: Antes era muy tímido, pero ahora es youtuber.

examples.en: There used to be a bookshop on this corner.
examples.es: Antes había una librería en esta esquina.

explain.title: ¿USED TO o PAST SIMPLE?
explain.es: Las dos hablan del pasado, pero used to es para hábitos y estados que duraron un tiempo y ya no son así (como el imperfecto: iba). Para una acción de una sola vez, una fecha concreta, cuántas veces o un periodo cerrado (for two years), usa el past simple (como el indefinido: fui).
explain.en: Used to = repeated habits / long states, now finished. One action, a date, a number of times or a fixed period → past simple.

cols.head: 🔁 used to · hábito / estado
items: I used to go to Italy every summer. (iba)
We used to play chess a lot. (jugábamos)

explain.title: 5 · ¿Y en presente? USUALLY
explain.es: En español decimos «suelo» en presente, pero used to solo existe en pasado. Para los hábitos de ahora usa el present simple, normalmente con usually: I use to get up at 7 → I usually get up at 7.
explain.en: Used to only exists in the past. For present habits use the present simple + usually.

examples.en: I used to get up at six when I lived in the country.
examples.es: Antes me levantaba a las seis, cuando vivía en el campo.

examples.en: She usually takes the bus, but she used to cycle.
examples.es: Normalmente coge el autobús, pero antes iba en bici.

explain.title: Expresiones que lo acompañan
head: Expresión
Significado
Ejemplo · Example
rows: When I was a kid, I used to collect stickers.
en el colegio / en la uni
At school, I used to sit at the back.
Years ago, people used to write letters.
Back then, we used to live in Vigo.
I used to smoke, but I don't any more.
These days, I hardly ever go out.
explain.note: Con used to no se dice cuántas veces ni una fecha exacta: I used to go there three times → I went there three times.
explain.note_en: Don't use used to with a number of times or an exact date.

explain.title: USED TO ≠ BE USED TO
explain.es: Solo para que no te líe: be used to + -ing significa «estar acostumbrado a» y puede ir en presente. Lo estudiarás a fondo más adelante; de momento, aprende a reconocerlo.
explain.en: be used to + -ing means «be accustomed to». It's different! Just learn to recognise it for now.

cols.head: 📼 used to + infinitivo
items: I used to live in London. (antes vivía)

cols.head: 💪 be used to + -ing
items: I'm used to living in London. (estoy acostumbrado)
She's used to working nights. (está acostumbrada)

items.es: ¿Es algo del pasado que se repetía o que duraba y ya no es así? → used to.
items.en: Past habit or state, not true now? → used to.

items.es: Afirmativa: sujeto + used to + infinitivo (igual para todos).
Negativa: didn't use to (¡sin d!) o never used to.
items.en: Negative: didn't use to / never used to.
Question: (Wh-) + did + subject + use to + verb?

items.es: ¿Es una sola vez, una fecha o un número de veces? → past simple. ¿Es un hábito de ahora? → usually.
items.en: One time → past simple. Present habit → usually.

lines.en: Grandad, is that you in this photo? You used to have so much hair!

lines.en: No TV and no phones? I couldn't live like that!
lines.es: ¿Sin tele y sin móviles? ¡Yo no podría vivir así!

lines.en: You'd be surprised. We used to be very happy!

explain.title: Truco: la regla de la D
explain.es: La d de used es la marca de pasado. Solo puede haber una marca de pasado por frase: si ya está did / didn't, la d desaparece. I used to… → I didn't use to… → Did you use to…? ¡Igual que I went → I didn't go!
explain.en: Only one past marker per sentence: with did / didn't, write use to (no -d).

exercises.title: Lee y contesta
exercises.es: Lee el texto. Marca T (verdadero) o F (falso) y contesta las preguntas con frases completas.
exercises.en: Read the text. Tick T or F and answer the questions.
text: My name is Marta and I grew up in Cangas, a small fishing town in Galicia. When I was a child, life there used to be very quiet. There didn't use to be many cars, so we used to play football in the street until it got dark.

My dad was a fisherman. He used to get up at four in the morning and he didn't use to come home until the afternoon. My mum used to sell his fish at the market. On Sundays, the whole family used to have lunch at my grandparents' house.

Things are very different now. There's a big supermarket where the market used to be, and in summer the town is full of tourists. I live in Madrid now and I usually visit Cangas twice a year. I love it, but I sometimes miss the old days.

items.q: When Marta was a child, there were a lot of cars in Cangas.
items.why: There didn't use to be many cars.

items.q: Her dad used to start work very early.
Her mum used to work at the market.
In summer, Cangas is still very quiet.
items.why: In summer the town is full of tourists.

items.q: Where did the children use to play football?
items.a: They used to play in the street.

items.q: What did the family use to do on Sundays?
items.a: They used to have lunch at her grandparents' house.

items.q: How often does Marta visit Cangas now?
items.a: She usually visits it twice a year.
